..
Another round of heavy rainfall is possible tonight for Guam and
Rota, so the previously-issued headline continues through tonight. 
Surface convergence continues to be concentrated south of the 
Marianas, so the zones remain split as drier air from the north will 
move over Saipan and Tinian Thursday morning before spreading to Guam
and Rota Thursday afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms remain in the 
forecast for quite some time as upper-level divergence is favorable 
over the entire region. Gentle to moderate west and northwest winds 
will decrease to light and variable on Thursday across the region. As
for the weekend, showers will be on and off, with Sunday and Monday 
looking to be the driest for Guam and Rota. On the other hand, a
col may set up over Saipan and Tinian, potentially bringing 
relatively dry conditions through the entire weekend. There is a 
large disagreement between the models regarding a potential tropical
disturbance developing west of the region, so showers top out at 30 
percent for the region due to the high uncertainty. Next week,
scattered showers may return for all islands.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 8 ft and will persist through the rest of the 
forecast period. There is a moderate risk of rip currents along all 
reefs as surf is elevated but still below hazardous criteria of 9 ft.
A couple of long-period swells are expected from the north and 
northeast due to distant tropical cyclones, as well as the 
continuation of the southwesterly monsoon swell. Light to moderate 
west to southwesterly winds will continue for Guam and Rota, with 
light and variable winds expected over Saipan and Tinian beginning 
Thursday.

Tropical Systems...
At 100 PM ChST, Tropical Storm Koguma was located 330 miles southwest 
of Wake Island near 16N164E, moving northeast at 10 mph. Koguma 
remains in an area of marginal support for development and is 
therefore expected to continue to only slowly strengthen as it 
continues moving west-northwest over the next few days, with a 
decrease in forward speed. TS Koguma could become a typhoon Thursday.

For more information on TS Koguma, please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
An overall dry pattern has moved into the region, with partly cloudy
skies and isolated showers expected at Majuro through the end of the
week, and at Pohnpei and Kosrae through the weekend. Majuro can 
expect to see a slight increase in showers, with POPs (Probability of
Precipitation) reaching around 30 percent Saturday night into 
Sunday. Otherwise, the dry pattern will continue into next week. For 
Pohnpei and Kosrae, POPs look to increase early next week as the 
monsoon trough begins to relocate back to the south, breaking away 
from TS Koguma. 

Benign marine conditions are expected to continue through the
beginning of next week, with combined seas subsiding to around 3 to 
4 feet by the weekend. Light to gentle winds will continue through
the weekend at Majuro, while gentle to moderate winds at Pohnpei and
Kosrae will become light to gentle for the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon surge remains the dominant feature in the region. This
feature is currently located over Palau and Yap, and producing 
scattered to widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms, and 10 
to 20 mph (10 to 15 kt) winds. QPF model guidance suggests about up 
to an inch of rain per day is possible for both islands. Overall, a 
wet week is to be expected with calmer winds.

Further to the east, Chuuk can expect a quite benign weather pattern
through the weekend as a ridge of high pressure has set up over the
region. 

Altimetry shows combined seas of 5 to 7 feet across the region, with
the highest to the east of Yap. Winds are expected to be gentle to 
moderate for Palau and Yap, while winds near Chuuk is expected to be
light to gentle. Overall, near the monsoon surge seas are expected 
to be elevated and choppy, then becoming more benign to the east. 
Seas near Palau and Yap are expected to gradually taper down by a 
foot by the beginning of next week. Seas near Chuuk are expected to 
remain steady through the weekend.
